patch_description:
The original implementation could corrupt rows and columns during recursive reconstruction: it created new DataFrames from value lists, used asynchronous completion order as row order, merged on a synthetic index, dropped/recreated columns, and finally returned an empty column-ordering list. This violates the required API because row-specific permutations cannot be interpreted without valid per-row orderings, and mixed/missing values may be altered by pandas reconstruction.

The replacement preserves every original value, row, index, and shape. It builds a small bounded set of column-order candidates, measures their actual serialized Trie-prefix reuse using sorted-string LCP scoring, and returns the best candidate together with valid per-row column orderings. It supports mixed values and missing values without changing stored data, honors merge/dependency ordering constraints, and avoids the unsafe recursive DataFrame mutation paths.
